events.name: Saint Nicholas Parade
events.place: Sedan (FR), rue de la Linette → Théâtre des Nutons
events.description: An illuminated procession with storytelling scenes along the route, after which every child meets Saint Nicholas; hot chocolate and mulled wine in a festively decorated courtyard.
events.coords_note: coordinates of Sedan town centre (place d'Armes), not of rue de la Linette

events.name: Arlon Charity Christmas Market
events.place: Arlon, place Léopold (in a heated marquee)
events.description: Chalets and charity stalls in a heated marquee in the heart of Belgium's oldest town; free entry.

events.name: Sedan Christmas Market
events.place: Sedan (FR), place d'Armes and place de la Halle
events.description: More than two weeks of chalets at the foot of the largest fortified castle in Europe; free entry.

events.name: Virton Christmas Market
events.place: Virton, place Nestor Outer and avenue Bouvier
events.description: The big Christmas market of Gaume's "capital", 15 minutes from the house: craftspeople, mulled wine and local Gaume produce.

events.name: Bouillon Christmas Market
events.place: Bouillon, at the foot of the castle
events.description: One of the best-known Christmas markets in the province, set up at the foot of Godfrey's fortress.
events.coords_note: quai des Saulx; exact location varies from year to year

events.name: Night-time Magic at the Euro Space Center
events.description: A special evening when the space centre is decked out with lights and family activities during the winter holidays.

events.name: Castle Trail Bouillon
events.description: A winter trail run through the loops of the Semois around the castle, over three distances.
events.note: dates published by trail-running calendars, not yet by the organiser

events.name: Arlon Carnival
events.dates: late February or early March (28 February 2027 according to a third-party listing; 5-8 March in 2026)
events.description: Carnival procession, traditional "soumonces" and brass bands in the streets of the provincial capital.

events.name: Great Bonfires of Gaume (e.g. the Grand Feu de Vance)
events.dates: late February to late March, date varies from village to village
events.description: A Walloon tradition: huge bonfires lit at the end of winter to "burn" the bad season away, often with a bar and a lively village atmosphere.
events.coords_note: approximate coordinates of the village of Vance

events.name: Florenville Flower Carnival
events.description: A cavalcade of floats covered in some 400,000 paper flowers, with Guggenmusik and brass bands; recognised as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation.

events.name: Gaume Jazz "Ibiyewa" (Jazz Tour)
events.place: Rossignol-Tintigny Cultural Centre, rue Camille Joset 1
events.description: A Brussels trio blending African rhythms, groove and improvisation (Angelo Moustapha, Toine Thys, Joel Rabesolo), 10 minutes from the house.

events.name: Philosophers' Walk in Gaume (11th edition)
events.place: Gaume villages, usually starting around Chassepierre
events.dates: a dozen days between 7 and 18 April 2027 (stages not yet published)
events.description: A travelling arts hike: each evening brings a performance or gathering in a different Gaume village, organised by the Chassepierre Festival.
events.note: period confirmed by the official call for projects; 2027 host villages not yet known

events.name: Les Aralunaires
events.place: Arlon (halls and unusual venues in the town centre)
events.dates: late April - early May, 5 days (29 April - 3 May in 2026)
events.description: A contemporary music festival that takes over unusual venues across Arlon, with free aperitif concerts.

events.name: Sedan Medieval Festival
events.dates: mid-May, one weekend (15-16 May 2027 estimated; 16-17 May in 2026)
events.description: Europe's largest fortified castle hosts medieval camps, combat displays, craftspeople and banquets.

events.name: Maitrank Festival
events.dates: a weekend in late May, 3 days (22-24 May in 2026)
events.description: A celebration of Arlon's aperitif made from white wine and sweet woodruff: induction ceremonies, concerts and tastings around town.

events.name: Chiny Summer Fêtes at the Château du Faing
events.dates: Sundays in late June and July (2027 programme not yet published)
events.description: Free afternoons in the castle park: street bands, big bands, vintage cars and refreshment stalls run by local associations, 3 km from the house.
events.coords_note: rue du Faing in Jamoigne, approximate

events.name: Festival Trail Semois
events.dates: early July, one Saturday (4 July in 2026)
events.description: Trail runs, canicross, walks and children's races in the Herbeumont forests, raising money for local charities.

events.name: Chiny Intercultural Storytelling Festival
events.dates: a weekend in mid-July, 2 days (11-12 July in 2026)
events.description: More than 80 shows and activities in the "City of Tales", including storytelling trips by boat on the Semois.

events.name: Libramont Agricultural Fair
events.description: Western Europe's major agricultural, forestry and food fair: livestock, machinery and local produce.

events.name: Gaume Jazz Festival
events.description: A renowned jazz festival in a shady park: some twenty Belgian and international concerts in a family-friendly atmosphere.

events.name: Bouillon Medieval Festival
events.dates: a weekend in mid-August (39th edition in 2026)
events.description: Bouillon travels back to the Middle Ages: camps, knights, craftspeople and shows at the foot of Godfrey's castle.

events.name: Chassepierre International Street Arts Festival
events.description: The village becomes an open-air stage: some 25,000 spectators come to see companies from all over the world.

events.name: Orval Trail
events.dates: late August, one Sunday (23 August in 2026)
events.description: A trail run through the forests between Muno and the Orval area.
events.note: information taken from a third-party calendar, to be checked

events.name: Wallonia Heritage Days
events.place: All over Wallonia (in 2026: free visits to the Montauban-Buzenol lapidary museum)
events.description: Hundreds of monuments open free of charge, often with guided tours and demonstrations.

events.name: Rochehaut Oktoberfest
events.dates: late September and early October, 2 weekends (25-27 Sept. and 9-11 Oct. in 2026)
events.description: Bavarian atmosphere, local beers and music above the famous Frahan viewpoint.

events.name: Halloween at Bouillon Castle
events.description: Underground passages and ramparts open to visitors in fancy dress, haunted by ghosts and creatures for a spine-chilling evening.

events.name: Virton European Film Festival
events.dates: first half of November, about 10 days
events.description: A European film festival founded in 1980, with its Belgian cinema day on the first Sunday.

events.name: Winter Delights – Florenville Christmas Market
events.dates: late November, one weekend (28-30 November for the 1st edition, 2025)
events.description: Christmas market run by Florenville's shopkeepers in a heated marquee, with a parade.

events.name: Halle de Han Farmers' Market
events.dates: every Friday 5-8 pm, all year round (bar-restaurant until 10.30 pm)
events.description: The only covered producers' market in the province open all year round: 20 to 30 Gaume producers, and you can eat on site.

events.name: Chassepierre Farmers' Market
events.description: A small producers' market in one of the most beautiful villages in Wallonia, perfect before a walk along the Semois.

events.name: Virton Weekly Market
events.description: Gaume's big weekly market, with plenty of stalls.

events.name: Jamoigne Farmers' Market
events.place: Jamoigne (Chiny), square in front of the post office
events.description: A producers' market 3 km from the house.

events.name: Bouillon Sunday Market
events.dates: every Sunday 8 am-1 pm, from late March to late October (29 March - 25 October in 2026)
events.description: A tourist market with around 50 stallholders on the banks of the Semois.

places.name: Orval Abbey of Notre-Dame (ruins and museums)
places.description: A Trappist abbey where you can visit the listed medieval ruins, the Matilda Fountain and the museums housed in the cellars; shop selling Orval beer, cheese and bread.
places.tip: The brewery and the modern abbey are closed to visitors (monastic enclosure): plan instead on the shop and the cheese, which is matured on site.

places.name: À l'Ange Gardien (Orval)
places.description: The abbey's tavern-restaurant, opposite the entrance: Orval cheese boards, Gaume pâté and Trappist beers.
places.tip: It is the only place serving "Petite Orval" (Green Orval) on draught, a lighter beer brewed for the monks.

places.name: Chiny, "City of Tales"
places.description: The former seat of the Counts of Chiny on the banks of the Semois, now the City of Tales thanks to its storytelling festival; historical walks start from the Church of St Walburga.
places.tip: The tourist office (061 31 54 04) runs "In the footsteps of medieval Chiny" walks; see conte.be for the Storytelling Nights.
places.note: the City of Tales' 2027 winter programme has not yet been published

places.name: Boat trip down the Semois (Chiny → Lacuisine)
places.description: Boatmen punt large flat-bottomed boats some 8-9 km between cliffs and forests, from Chiny to Lacuisine.
places.tip: Book in high season and ask whether the shuttle back is included; around €25 for a single seat, €50 for a two-seater according to a 2026 guide.
places.coords_note: landing-stage area (rue de l'Embarcadère, Chiny), approximate

places.name: Kayaking on the Semois from Chiny
places.description: Several hire companies in Chiny (L'Embarcadère, Le Batifol) offer Chiny–Lacuisine, Chiny–Florenville or Chiny–Chassepierre trips.
places.tip: Chiny–Florenville (about 2 hours, ~€20) is the best compromise; check the water level, as trips depend on the river's flow.

places.name: Rocher du Hât (Chiny)
places.description: A rocky viewpoint above the Semois, near the Chiny landing stage.
places.tip: Combine it with the riverside path between the landing stage and the Saint-Nicolas bridge.

places.name: Chassepierre, one of the most beautiful villages in Wallonia
places.description: A slate-stone village on the Semois, with its Church of St Martin (1702) in an old walled churchyard and a viewpoint over a loop of the river.
places.tip: Stop at the viewpoint on the Florenville–Bouillon road (viewpoint indicator, picnic tables), then walk down to the Trou des Fées (Fairies' Hole) below the church.

places.name: Florenville viewpoint (church and panoramic tower)
places.description: Behind the church, a landscaped viewpoint overlooks the Semois valley; the 50 m tower offers an 800 km² panorama.
places.tip: The viewpoint behind the church is open at all times; the tower opens daily only in July-August and occasionally the rest of the year.
places.coords_note: place Albert Ier, next to the church

places.name: Sainte-Cécile suspension footbridge
places.description: A 185 m suspension footbridge nearly 30 m above the Semois, opened on 20 June 2026, between the forests of Sainte-Cécile and Les Épioux.
places.tip: Accessible on foot only; combine it with the Rocher du Chat on a waymarked circular walk.
places.coords_note: starting point/car park in Sainte-Cécile, not the footbridge itself

places.name: Herbeumont Castle ruins
places.description: Medieval ruins on a ridge with views of the Semois winding its loops between cliffs and forests.
places.tip: Free access from the castle car park; the Tombeau du Chevalier loop (about 6 km) starts here.

places.name: Tombeau du Géant (Botassart)
places.description: The most famous viewpoint on the Semois: the river wraps around a wooded hill shaped like a tomb.
places.tip: Park in Botassart and walk down towards the Moulin du Rivage; the best time is late in the day, when low sunlight sweeps across the loop.
places.coords_note: OSM viewpoint (Point de vue du Châteaumont, Botassart); the hill itself is around 49.8138, 5.0424

places.name: Bouillon Castle
places.description: A medieval fortress on three rocky spurs overlooking the Semois, strengthened by Vauban; underground passages and falconry shows.
places.tip: The "Bouillon City Pass" combines the castle, the Ducal Museum and the Bouillon Medieval Experience; falconry shows run from early March to mid-November.

places.name: Archéoscope – Bouillon Medieval Experience
places.description: An immersive show about Godfrey of Bouillon and the Crusades, at the foot of the castle.
places.tip: Ideal on a rainy day; included in the Bouillon City Pass, so check before buying separate tickets.

places.name: Frahan viewpoint (Rochehaut)
places.description: The most photographed view in the Ardennes: the hamlet of Frahan in a loop of the Semois.
places.tip: Free access by car or on foot; spectacular in autumn, and the Brasserie de Rochehaut is 300 m away.

places.name: Rochehaut Wildlife Park
places.description: Nearly 300 animals from the Ardennes and Europe on 40 ha, seen from a little train above the loop of the Semois; Agri-Musée next door.
places.tip: The little train (about 1½ hours) passes a view over Frahan; check the day's departure times, as they vary with the weather.

places.name: Torgny, "Belgium's little Provence"
places.description: Belgium's southernmost village, built of ochre stone and listed among the Most Beautiful Villages of Wallonia, with vineyards and its own microclimate.
places.tip: Climb up to the Raymond Mayné nature reserve, Belgium's first nature reserve, for its Mediterranean flora and the view over Lorraine.

places.name: Montauban archaeological site and lapidary museum (Buzenol)
places.description: A fortified spur occupied for fifteen centuries, with a museum of Gallo-Roman bas-reliefs, including the famous "vallus", the harvesting machine of the Treveri.
places.tip: Opening hours vary: check with the Maison du Tourisme de Gaume (063 39 31 00); the harvester is demonstrated during the Heritage Days.
places.coords_note: rue de Montauban in Buzenol, approximate

places.name: Avioth Basilica (France)
places.description: A Flamboyant Gothic basilica standing alone in the Lorraine countryside, with the "Recevresse", a unique little shrine where offerings were left.
places.tip: 15 minutes from the house: combine it with the nearby citadel of Montmédy.

places.name: Clairefontaine Abbey ruins (Arlon)
places.description: Ruins of the burial place of the Counts of Luxembourg, founded by Countess Ermesinde, and a neo-Romanesque chapel in a wooded valley.
places.tip: Volunteers (Amanoclair) offer guided tours; check the dates on arlon-clairefontaine.com.

places.name: Conchibois Lake (Saint-Léger)
places.description: A leisure lake in unspoilt Gaume countryside, promoted as a bathing spot with good water quality, with a car park and walks starting from it.
places.tip: Check with Saint-Léger council whether swimming is open and supervised before going with children.
places.note: lifeguard supervision and bathing season not confirmed

places.name: Euro Space Center (Transinne)
places.description: A space discovery centre: simulators (including Mars Explorer, new in 2026), exhibitions and activities, mostly indoors.
places.tip: Book online (€2 off each ticket) and arrive early: last entry is around 4 pm, and you need a full day.

places.name: Rulles craft brewery
places.description: A renowned Gaume brewery (Rulles Blonde, Triple, Estivale…), with an adjoining shop.
places.tip: Guided tours with tastings take place on set dates or for group bookings (visite@larulles.be): enquire beforehand.

places.name: Gengoulf Brewery (Villers-devant-Orval)
places.description: An artisan microbrewery a stone's throw from Orval.
places.tip: No shop with fixed opening hours: call (+32 494 18 14 45) or email contact@gengoulf.be before you go.

places.name: Halle de Han (Tintigny)
places.description: A covered producers' market open every Friday evening: cheeses, charcuterie, vegetables, bread and Gaume beers.
places.tip: Come at 5 pm for the best choice, then have dinner on site: the bar-restaurant stays open until 10.30 pm.

places.name: Fromagerie du Marronnier (Muno)
places.description: An organic farm selling its own raw cow's and goat's milk products: milk, butter, cream, soft and hard cheeses.
places.tip: Call ahead (061 32 06 54): sales and farm visits are by appointment or at limited times.
places.coords_note: rue Watrinsart, Muno; house number 23 not precisely located

places.name: Virton Aquatic Centre
places.description: An indoor pool open all year round, with a 25 m lap pool and a leisure pool: the closest to the house in winter.
places.tip: Closed on Sundays and Mondays during term time; check the holiday opening hours on piscinevirton.be.

places.name: Le Florenville campsite pool (summer)
places.description: A heated outdoor pool open to the public, with no need to stay at the campsite.
places.tip: Open roughly from mid-May to mid-September; about €13 per adult according to a 2026 guide, to be confirmed.

places.name: Musée gaumais (Virton)
places.description: In the former Recollect friary, 2,000 years of Gaume history and folk art: cast-iron fireback plates, period interiors, tools and religious art.
places.tip: Free entry on the first Sunday of the month; check the closing day (sources disagree between Monday and Tuesday).

places.name: Sedan Castle (France)
places.description: Often billed as the largest fortified castle in Europe (35,000 m²), with a self-guided route and audio guide.
places.tip: Entry around €12 in 2026; you can even stay the night, as a hotel occupies the former Fabert storehouses.

places.name: Chameleux Gallo-Roman site (Florenville)
places.description: Remains of a staging post on the Roman road from Reims to Trier, occupied from the 1st to the 5th century, on the way to Orval.
places.tip: 5 minutes from the abbey: stop here before or after Orval.

places.name: Roche à l'Appel and the "Luna and the Forest Guardians" trail (Muno)
places.description: A chaos of conglomerate rocks in a nature reserve, with a digital trail for children.
places.tip: Sturdy shoes recommended: the rocks are slippery after rain.

places.name: Château du Faing park (Jamoigne)
places.description: The wooded castle park in Jamoigne, home to the Chiny Summer Fêtes.
places.tip: 3 km from the house, it makes an easy stroll at the end of the day.
